今天的主题：环境污染和健康研究（微塑料）。这组词是雅思高频话题：大作文常考「塑料污染该由政府还是个人负责」「该不该禁止一次性塑料」；阅读和听力 Part 4 的科普讲座爱用 evidence、data、correlation、exposure 这类词；口语 Part 3 问环保习惯时也能直接用。强化期第 4 天，每个词后面 ≈ 是同义替换，雅思听力和阅读最爱把原文换个说法出题，背的时候连同义词一起记。

例句

  • There is growing evidence that microplastics are harmful to marine life.（越来越多的证据表明微塑料对海洋生物有害。）
  • Researchers found a strong correlation between air pollution and asthma.（研究人员发现空气污染和哮喘之间有很强的相关性。）
  • Long-term exposure to toxic chemicals can damage your health.（长期接触有毒化学品会损害健康。）
  • Governments should encourage people to reduce their consumption of disposable plastic.（政府应该鼓励人们减少一次性塑料的使用。）
  • Sales of bottled water saw a spike during the heatwave.（热浪期间瓶装水的销量激增。）

同义替换小抄（听力最常见的考法）：

题目写 link / connection → 录音可能说 correlation　|　题目写 sharp rise → 录音说 spike　|　题目写 sea creatures → 录音说 marine animals　|　题目写 swallow / take in → 录音说 ingest　|　题目写 measured → 录音说 quantified　|　题目写 new / developing → 录音说 emerging

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，并能说出至少 15 个词的一个同义替换。再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 reduce、disposable、harmful 写一句「政府应该限制一次性塑料」，大作文能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Are microplastics harming us?（微塑料在伤害我们吗？），11 月 19 日刚出的新一期。Phil 和 Becca 聊肉眼看不见的微塑料怎么通过食物进入人体，中间有两段真实采访（肝病专家 Shilpa Chokshi 和材料科学教授 Mark Miodownik），最后给了几个减少接触的生活小建议。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。官方雅思样题这周已经做完了，今天在 BBC 节目后面加了一组我按雅思格式出的笔记填空题（Q1–8），练强化期的听写和同义替换。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，像考试一样做下面的笔记填空 Q1–8，只听一遍，边听边写，听完点「对答案」。
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。两段采访语速快、有 you know 这种口头禅，最难，可以先读懂中文再听。
  4. 第三遍挑 Phil 讲尼龙工厂那段（"Well, plastics have been a big part of daily life since the 1950s..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：marine（海洋的）、emerging（新出现的）、correlation（相关性）、spike（激增）、quantified（量化的）、exposure（接触）。

笔记填空 Questions 1–8（按雅思格式自编）

Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

Microplastics and our health

• Social media claim: we ingest a credit card's worth of plastic every 1

• In fact, this would take about 2 years

• One of the main food groups containing microplastics: 3

• Prof. Chokshi saw plastic in the 4 and guts of sea creatures

• Plastics have been part of daily life since the 5

• Scientists are studying people who worked in 6 factories

• Prof. Miodownik: the amount of plastic 7 in supermarkets keeps rising

• Tip: replace tea bags with 8 tea

答案：1 week　2 23,000　3 seafood　4 livers（liver 也算对）　5 1950s　6 nylon　7 packaging　8 loose-leaf。同义替换提示：题目 sea creatures = 录音 marine animals；题目 keeps rising = 录音 gone up and up；题目 In fact = 录音 I'm afraid it's only。

点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Phil：Hi Becca.

Phil：你好，贝卡。

Becca：Hi Phil.

Becca：你好，菲尔。

Phil：Becca, I've got a question for you. What's the last plastic thing you had in your hands?

Phil：贝卡，问你个问题。你最近一次拿在手里的塑料东西是什么？

Becca：Well, I just did my makeup化妆；化妆品, so probably a makeup化妆；化妆品 brush.

Becca：嗯，我刚化完妆，所以大概是化妆刷吧。

Phil：Many of us own lots of things made of plastic. It's cheap, easy to shape and long lasting, but that's not always a good thing. In this episode of 6 Minute English, we'll be hearing from experts as they teach us about microplastics – those are tiny plastic pieces. And we'll be asking the question, 'Are microplastics affecting our health?' OK. Well, let's start with our quiz, Becca. There was a social media post that says that every week we ingest摄入，吃进 the same amount of plastic as there is in a credit card信用卡, but that's not true.

Phil：我们很多人都有一大堆塑料做的东西。塑料便宜、容易塑形、又耐用，但这并不总是好事。这一期《六分钟英语》，我们会听专家讲讲微塑料，也就是非常小的塑料碎片。我们要问的问题是：「微塑料在影响我们的健康吗？」好，贝卡，先来做小测验。社交媒体上有个帖子说，我们每周吃进去的塑料相当于一张信用卡那么多，但这不是真的。

Becca：Oh, thank goodness谢天谢地!

Becca：哦，谢天谢地！

Phil：So, my question for you is how long would it really take to ingest摄入，吃进 that amount of microplastics? Would it be:
a) 13,000 years,
b) 23,000 years, or
c) 33,000 years?

Phil：所以我的问题是：真要吃进那么多微塑料，实际需要多长时间？是 a) 1.3 万年，b) 2.3 万年，还是 c) 3.3 万年？

Becca：Well, I want to be hopeful, so I'll go with the longest period of time. That would be 33,000 years.

Becca：嗯，我想乐观一点，所以选最长的，3.3 万年。

Phil：OK. Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.

Phil：好，节目最后揭晓答案。

Becca：So, the World Health Organisation says that microplastics have been found in many different food groups. But Phil, what is the food group that is more affected by microplastics?

Becca：世界卫生组织说，很多类食物里都发现了微塑料。菲尔，那哪一类食物受微塑料影响更严重呢？

Phil：Well, scientists have found that seafood海鲜 is one of the main food groups where microplastics can be found, and BBC World Service programme The Evidence证据 has been investigating调查 this. Professor Shilpa Chokshi told host Claudia Hammond about some pictures that she was shown by a microplastics expert.

Phil：科学家发现，海鲜是含有微塑料的主要食物类别之一。BBC 国际台的节目《The Evidence》一直在调查这件事。希尔帕·乔克希教授跟主持人克劳迪娅·哈蒙德讲了一位微塑料专家给她看的一些照片。

Professor Shilpa Chokshi：And he showed me all these marine海洋的 animals that looked like they had plastics in their livers肝脏 and hind guts后肠. And from that initial最初的 discussion, I went away and I looked at the literature（某领域的）文献 and I looked at the data, and there was emerging新出现的，新兴的 evidence证据 that there was plastics in the liver肝脏, and there was this correlation相关性，关联 increase.

Professor Shilpa Chokshi：他给我看了好多海洋动物，看起来它们的肝脏和后肠里都有塑料。那次最初的讨论之后，我回去查了文献、看了数据，发现有新出现的证据表明肝脏里有塑料，而且这种相关性还在增加。

Becca：Shilpa says that plastics have been found in marine海洋的 animals. Marine海洋的 describes anything related to, found in or produced by the sea.

Becca：希尔帕说在海洋动物体内发现了塑料。marine 用来形容任何和海有关、在海里发现或由海产生的东西。

Phil：Yes, these pictures of marine海洋的 animals with plastics in their bodies inspired激励，促使 Shilpa to dive deeper into更深入地研究 the data. She found emerging新出现的，新兴的 evidence证据, and the adjective emerging新出现的，新兴的 describes something coming into view开始显现，进入视野 after being hidden, allowing it to develop or be better understood.

Phil：对，这些体内有塑料的海洋动物照片促使希尔帕更深入地研究数据。她发现了新出现的证据。形容词 emerging 指原本看不到的东西开始显现出来，从而能进一步发展或被更好地理解。

Becca：And from this emerging新出现的，新兴的 evidence证据, Shilpa noticed a correlation相关性，关联. You'll hear this word a lot when talking about data. A correlation相关性，关联 is a link or connection between two or more things. So, Phil, we know how toxic有毒的 microplastics get into our body, but are they definitely harmful有害的?

Becca：从这些新证据里，希尔帕注意到了一种相关性。谈数据的时候你会经常听到这个词。correlation 指两个或多个事物之间的联系。那么菲尔，我们知道有毒的微塑料是怎么进入身体的了，但它们一定有害吗？

Phil：Well, plastics have been a big part of daily life since the 1950s, but it's only recently that we've started thinking about microplastics as a health issue. For example, scientists have been looking at people who worked in nylon尼龙 factories where they were exposed使接触，使暴露 to high levels of microplastic. And the scientists think that there may be a correlation相关性，关联 between this and diseases that they developed later on. Science professor Mark Miodownik, from University College London, has mixed feelings复杂的心情，又喜又忧 about microplastics and explained these to BBC World Service programme The Evidence证据.

Phil：从上世纪 50 年代起，塑料就是日常生活的重要部分了，但直到最近我们才开始把微塑料当成健康问题来看。比如，科学家一直在研究曾在尼龙工厂工作的人，他们接触过高浓度的微塑料。科学家认为这和他们后来得的病之间可能存在相关性。伦敦大学学院的科学教授马克·米奥多尼克对微塑料的看法比较复杂，他在 BBC 国际台的节目《The Evidence》里解释了原因。

Professor Mark Miodownik：Well, you know, we have been exposed使接触，使暴露 for decades十年 and surely if it was that bad, you know, we'd have seen a spike激增，急剧增加 or something by now. But on the other hand另一方面, you know, I think, you know, if you look at how much plastic packaging包装 is in supermarkets, it's gone up and up and up and up. And this is not a quantified量化，用数字衡量 measure, but our exposure接触，暴露 seems to be increasing, and that's the worry for me.

Professor Mark Miodownik：嗯，你知道，我们已经接触了几十年，如果真有那么糟，到现在肯定早该看到某种激增了。但另一方面，我觉得，你看看超市里有多少塑料包装，一直在涨、涨、涨。这不是量化过的数据，但我们的接触量似乎在增加，这才是让我担心的地方。

Becca：Mark mentions that some people say if microplastics were harmful有害的, we surely would have seen a spike激增，急剧增加 in issues related to them by now. A spike激增，急剧增加 is literally a pointy shape, but here it means a sudden, sharp increase in something.

Becca：马克提到，有人说如果微塑料有害，到现在我们肯定已经看到相关问题激增了。spike 字面意思是尖尖的形状，但这里指某样东西突然急剧增加。

Phil：Right. And though the amount of plastic packaging包装 we use has increased, this isn't a quantified量化，用数字衡量 measure. If something is quantified量化，用数字衡量, then it's measured and given a number or a value.

Phil：对。虽然我们用的塑料包装变多了，但这不是量化的数据。quantified 就是被测量过、给出了具体数字或数值。

Becca：So, Mark concludes得出结论 that he is worried about our exposure接触，暴露 to plastics. Exposure接触，暴露 means coming into contact with接触到 something that may have an impact on对……有影响 you. OK. Phil, so, if people are worried about their exposure接触，暴露 to microplastics, what can they do to reduce this?

Becca：所以马克的结论是，他担心我们对塑料的接触。exposure 指接触到可能对你产生影响的东西。好，菲尔，如果大家担心接触微塑料，可以做些什么来减少呢？

Phil：Well, one thing they can do is to replace things like plastic chopping boards砧板，菜板, utensils（厨房）用具 and food storage containers食品收纳盒. And another tip from BBC World Service's The Evidence证据 is to replace tea bags茶包, which often contain microplastics, with loose-leaf tea散装茶叶（不是茶包）. OK. Becca, now it's time to get the answer to our quiz question. And I asked you how long it would take to ingest摄入，吃进 a credit-card-sized amount of microplastics.

Phil：一个办法是换掉塑料砧板、厨房用具和食品收纳盒这类东西。《The Evidence》的另一个建议是：茶包里常常含有微塑料，可以改喝散装茶叶。好，贝卡，该揭晓小测验答案了。我问你吃进一张信用卡那么多的微塑料需要多久。

Becca：Yes, and I said 33,000 years.

Becca：对，我说的是 3.3 万年。

Phil：OK. Well, I've got two bits of bad news for you, Becca. One, you were wrong. And two, I'm afraid it's only 23,000 years that it would take to ingest摄入，吃进 that plastic. OK. Let's recap回顾，概括 the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with marine海洋的, which describes anything related to, found in or produced by the sea.

Phil：好，贝卡，我有两个坏消息。第一，你答错了。第二，恐怕吃进那么多塑料只需要 2.3 万年。好，我们来回顾一下这期学的词，先是 marine，形容和海有关、在海里发现或由海产生的东西。

Becca：The adjective emerging新出现的，新兴的 describes something coming into view开始显现，进入视野 after being hidden, allowing it to develop or be better understood.

Becca：形容词 emerging 指原本隐藏的东西开始显现，从而能进一步发展或被更好地理解。

Phil：A correlation相关性，关联 is a relationship between two or more things.

Phil：correlation 指两个或多个事物之间的关系。

小练习

  1. Scientists found a strong ______ between sleep and memory.（相关性）
  2. There was a ______ in ticket sales after the film won an award.（激增）
  3. Whales and dolphins are ______ animals.（海洋的）
  4. Long-term ______ to loud noise can damage your hearing.（接触）
  5. The benefits are hard to ______ because they are not financial.（量化）
  6. There is ______ evidence that the drug may help older patients.（新出现的）
点开看答案

开头那题选 b，2.3 万年，贝卡猜 3.3 万年，猜错了。填空：1. correlation 2. spike 3. marine 4. exposure 5. quantify 6. emerging

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 3 和大作文做准备）：Should governments ban single-use plastics? 用英语说两三句：I believe ... because ... / For example, ...。也可以想想：你家里哪些东西是塑料的？你会为了环保换成别的材料吗？
